question.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{5}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $5$ | $25$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{5}^{25}\frac{3}{x{log}_{5}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{5}^{25}\frac{1}{{log}_{5}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =3{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡5{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡5(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡5(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡2\operatorname{ln}⁡5\end{aligned}
$$
